paragraphs: So, here's the scoop from God, delivered to Hosea, son of Beeri. This all went down while Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah were running things in Judah, and Jeroboam son of Joash was king in Israel.
The very first thing God ever said to Hosea was pretty wild.
He said, “Go find a prostitute and marry her. Make her the mother of your children. And here’s the reason: this entire country has become a giant brothel, cheating on me, their God.”
And Hosea just... did it. He went and married Gomer, the daughter of Diblaim. She got pregnant and had a son.
Then God told him:

“Name that kid Jezreel. It won’t be long before I make the whole nation of Israel answer for the massacre that happened at Jezreel. I’m officially calling it quits on the kingdom of Israel. Payday is coming, and I’m going to chop their bows and arrows into kindling in the Valley of Jezreel.”
Gomer got pregnant again, and this time it was a girl. God told Hosea:

“Name her No-Mercy. I am so over Israel. I’ve run out of mercy. There are no more second chances. Judah, though, that’s a different situation. I’ll keep having mercy on them. I’ll save them. And it’ll be me, their God, who does the saving—not their military, not their weapons, not their cavalry or their soldiers.”
After Gomer had weaned No-Mercy, she got pregnant yet again and had another son. God said:
“Name him Nobody. Because you all have become nobodies to me, and I, God, am a nobody to you.”

“But hold up, plot twist. Down the road, the population of Israel is going to explode. You won’t even be able to count them, like grains of sand on the beach. And in the exact spot where they were called ‘Nobody,’ they’ll be called ‘God’s Somebody.’ Everyone from Judah and Israel will get back together as one crew. They’ll pick a single leader and become an unstoppable force. That’s gonna be a huge day for Jezreel!”

paragraphs: “Yo, rename your brothers ‘God’s Somebody.’ Rename your sisters ‘All Mercy.’

“Seriously, haul your mother into court — accuse her! She’s not my wife anymore, and I’m not her husband. Tell her to quit dressing like a prostitute, putting herself on display. If she refuses, I’ll rip her clothes off and expose her, naked as a newborn. I’ll turn her skin into dried-out leather, her body into a desert wasteland, nothing but bones. I’ll have nothing to do with her children, born one and all in that brothel. Face it: your mother’s been unfaithful, bringing illegitimate children into the world. She said, ‘I’m off to see my lovers! They’ll wine and dine me, dress and caress me, perfume and adorn me!’ But I’ll fix her: I’ll dump her in a field of thistles, then lose her in a dead-end alley. She’ll go hunting for her lovers but won’t catch a single one. She’ll look high and low but won’t find one. Then she’ll say, ‘I’m going back to my husband, the one I started out with. That was a better life by far.’ She never knew it was me all along who wined and dined and adorned her — I was the one who dressed her up in big-city fashion and jewelry, and she wasted it all on wild Baal-orgies. I’m about to bring her up short: no more wining and dining! Silk lingerie and gowns are a thing of the past. I’ll shame her in public, right in front of her lovers — all her fly-by-night lovers will be helpless to help her. Party time is over. I’m calling a halt to the whole thing: her wild weekends and unholy holidays. I’ll wreck her fancy gardens and ornamental fountains — she bragged, ‘My cheating paid for all this!’ They’ll soon be garbage dumps, feeding grounds for stray dogs and cats. I’ll make her pay for her reckless religion — all that wild Baal worship and all the cheating that went with it, stalking her lovers, dressed to kill, with not a single thought for me.” God’s Message!

“But get this — I’m going to start all over again. I’m taking her back out into the wilderness, where we had our first date, and I’ll court her. I’ll give her bouquets of roses. I’ll turn Heartbreak Valley into Acres of Hope. She’ll respond like she did as a young girl, back when she was fresh out of Egypt.

“At that time” — this is God’s Message still — “you’ll call me ‘Dear husband!’ Never again will you call me ‘My slave-master!’ I’ll wash your mouth out with soap and get rid of all those dirty false-god names — you won’t even whisper them again. And at the same time I’ll make a peace treaty between you and the wild animals, the birds, and the reptiles, and get rid of all weapons of war. Think of it! Safe from beasts and bullies! And then I’ll marry you for good — forever! I’ll marry you true and proper, in love and tenderness. Yes, I’ll marry you and neither leave you nor let you go. You’ll know me, God, for who I really am.

“On the very same day, I’ll answer” — this is God’s Message — “I’ll answer the sky, and the sky will answer the earth; the earth will answer the grain, the wine, and the olive oil, and they’ll all answer Jezreel. I’ll plant her in the good earth. I’ll have mercy on No-Mercy. I’ll say to Nobody, ‘You’re my dear Somebody,’ and he’ll say, ‘You’re my God!’”

paragraphs: Then God was like, “Alright, do it all over again. Go get your wife back, even though she’s with her new guy. Yeah, your cheating wife. Love her the way I, God, love the Israelite people, even when they’re out there chasing every other god they see.”

God then told me, “Go out again and love a woman who’s sleeping with other men, just like I love Israelites — because even though I keep loving them, they go after other gods like everything’s fine. They even take gifts to their gods.”
Then you’ll sit there a long time, empty and alone — no lover, no friend. You’ll wait and you’ll wait for me. I’ll wait and wait for you.

Then the people of Israel will turn back to God. They’ll come running to God, their God, and to the Son of David, their king. They’ll come trembling, holy awe-struck — they’ll turn and come back, and want a taste of God’s goodness in the last days.

title: God Calls Out the Fakes

paragraphs: Yo, Israel, listen up! God's got a major bone to pick with everyone. He's like, 'Nobody's loyal. Nobody's got love. Nobody even gets me.' It's just non-stop cursing, lying, murder, stealing, and sleeping around. Total chaos, just one person getting iced after another. And because of all this, the whole country is basically crying. Everything's messed up—the animals, the birds, even the fish are just floating around, totally dead inside.

There’s no truth, no faithfulness, and no knowledge of God anywhere in this country! People are constantly cursing, lying, murdering, stealing, and cheating. One murder after another. The more this goes on, the worse it gets. Even the animals and birds and fish are getting so fed up they’re taking off!

“But don’t try to blame anyone else. Your priests are the main problem! You priests have rejected me, and my knowledge, my revelation, my holy Word. You’ve gotten too big for your britches. So I’ve gotten too big for you. I’m firing you as priests for good. You’ve turned your backs on God’s revelation, so now I’ll forget your children. “The more priests, the more sin. Your mother is as bad as you. You’ve traded God’s glory for the cheap thrills of prostitution. The more sex your people have with false gods, the more I’ll let them do. The worse their sin, the worse I’ll make it. They’ll eat their fill of it — eating the food offered to idols, but never getting enough. They’ll keep having sex with those false gods, but there won’t be any babies. Because they’ve abandoned God, they’ll end up empty-handed and impotent.”

You really messed up your own life, Israel—but don't you dare drag Judah down with you! Don't go to the sex-shrine at Gilgal, and stay away from that sin-city Bethel. And don't go around saying 'God bless' when you don't even mean it, just throwing His name around. Israel is being stubborn, like a mule that won't move. How is God supposed to lead them into a good place like a gentle lamb? Ephraim is literally addicted to his idols. Just let him be. Once the party's over, it's all about sex, sex, and more sex. They love their shameless, dirty lifestyle. But a storm is coming to snatch them up, and their whole sex-worshipping thing will leave them with nothing.

paragraphs: Alright, listen up, you priests! And pay attention, people of Israel! Royal family, you better be all ears too! You're supposed to be the ones in charge of justice, but what have you actually been doing? You've been taking advantage of people at Mizpah, scamming them on Tabor, and totally victimizing them at Shittim. So yeah, I'm about to bring the hammer down on all of you.

“Listen up, you priests! Watch out, Israel! Pay close attention, you kings! God is coming after you! You’re the ones responsible for all this mess at Mizpah and Tabor — those dirty traps you’ve been setting. But now I’m wising up to all your sneaky tricks and I’ll deal with you once and for all. I know where you’ve been, Israel. You can’t fool me. You’re an open book. Every breath you take is a prostitute’s breath — everything you do is an orgy. They can’t turn around, can’t come back to God, because every breath they take is a prostitute’s breath — prostitute-sickness has them in its grip. Your arrogance gives you away — you’ve fallen flat on your face. Israel’s fallen flat on its face. Judah will be right behind. They’ll come with sheep and cattle, but it won’t be enough. They won’t find God — not with things! God’s long gone from this place, totally done with them. “They’ve cheated on God. They’ve sired bastard offspring. But their party won’t last. Before you know it, they’ll be like sickly cattle, with a skin disease that spreads everywhere.”

Your arrogance is off the charts, and honestly, it's a public embarrassment. All of you—Israel, Ephraim, and Judah—are just stumbling around in your own guilt. And when you finally decide to get your act together and look for God again, it's gonna be too late. I, God, will be long gone. You've been disloyal to me for way too long, and now your country is full of the consequences. A massive plague is about to wreck your trashed land.

“Blow the shofar in Gibeah! Sound the bugle in Ramah! Sound the battle cry in Bethel! “You’re in for a fight, Benjamin! Ephraim is about to be destroyed on the day I take action. I’m telling the tribes of Israel that this is real. “The leaders of Judah are like crooks who move boundary markers. I’ll pour out my anger on them like a flash flood.”

“Ephraim is smashed to smithereens by the Assyrians — fickle and faithless before their neighbors. He had no faith in his own gods. He was just trying to get an inside track with the Assyrians, trying to get on their good side. But when Ephraim saw he was sick, and Judah saw his own tumorous condition, they went to Assyria for help. They hired the Assyrian king to fix things. But he can’t do anything about it! He can’t heal them! I’ll deal with Ephraim as a pus and with Judah as an oozing sore.”

Ephraim has been brutal, and now he's about to get brutalized himself—a taste of his own medicine. He was so obsessed with doing things his own useless way. Because of that, I'm going to be like an infection to Ephraim, and like a rot that destroys the house of Judah.

When Ephraim realized he was sick and Judah saw his nasty, infected sores, Ephraim ran off to Assyria for help from their 'great' king. But plot twist: he can't heal you. He can't fix the mess you're in.

I'm about to go full-on grizzly bear on Ephraim, and like a mama bear with cubs on Judah. I'll tear them to pieces, for real. No one can stop me. I'll drag them off, and no one will be able to rescue them. Then, I'll go back to my place and wait until they finally get a clue. When they finally hit rock bottom, maybe then they'll start looking for me.

paragraphs: “Come on, let’s go back to God. God’s the one who mauled us — but now God’s ready to heal us. God wounded us — but now God will put on bandages. In a day or two God will heal us. Then on the third day we’ll be right up on our feet with God at our side, and we’ll know what it’s like to really know God! We’ll know God as well as we know the dawn — we’ll know that God is coming, like winter rain, like spring rain, watering the fields.”

“What am I ever going to do with you? Oh, Ephraim! Oh, Judah! Your love evaporates in the morning dew, disappears like the morning fog. That’s why I’ve attacked them through my prophets and slaughtered them with my words — my judgment comes like lightning. I’m after love that lasts, not religion. I want you to know God, not go to more prayer meetings.

“They broke the covenant — just as they did at Adam. They betrayed me, ungrateful as ever. Gilead, crime city! Horrors on every street! As robbers ambush travelers, so gangs of priests murder people on their way to Shechem. They’re a bunch of no-good scoundrels.”
“But I’ve seen a sickening sight in Israel’s house: Ephraim acting like a religious prostitute, Israel stinking to high heaven — a religious whorehouse!”
And you're just as bad, Judah. You've been out here living wild. Well, guess what? It's harvest time.

paragraphs: “Every time I gave Israel a fresh start, wiped the slate clean and got them going again, Ephraim soon filled the slate with new sins, the treachery of Samaria written out in bold print. Two-faced and double-tongued, they steal you blind, pick you clean. It never crosses their mind that I keep account of their every crime. They’re mud-spattered head to toe with the residue of sin. I see who they are and what they’ve done.

“They entertain the king with their evil circus, delight the princes with their acrobatic lies. They’re a bunch of overheated adulterers, like an oven that holds its heat from the kneading of the dough to the rising of the bread.

“On the royal holiday the princes get drunk on wine and the frenzy of the mocking mob. They’re like wood stoves, red-hot with lust. Through the night their passion is banked; in the morning it blazes up, flames hungrily licking. Murderous and volcanic, they incinerate their rulers. Their kings fall one by one, and no one pays any attention to me.
“Ephraim mingles with the pagans, dissipating himself. Ephraim is half-baked. Strangers suck him dry but he doesn’t even notice. His hair has turned gray — he doesn’t notice.
“Bloated by arrogance, big as a house, Israel’s a public disgrace. Israel lumbers along oblivious to God, despite all the signs, ignoring God.

“Ephraim is bird-brained, mindless, clueless, first chirping after Egypt, then fluttering after Assyria. I’ll throw my net over them. I’ll clip their wings. I’ll teach them to mind me! Doom! They’ve run away from home. Now they’re really in trouble! They’ve defied me. And I’m supposed to help them while they feed me a line of lies? Instead of crying out to me in heartfelt prayer, they whoop it up in bed with prostitutes, gash themselves bloody in their sex-and-religion orgies, but turn their backs on me. I’m the one who gave them good minds and healthy bodies, and how am I repaid? With evil scheming! They turn, but not to me — turn here, then there, like a weather vane. Their rulers will be cut down, murdered — just deserts for their mocking blasphemies. And the final sentence? Ridicule in the court of world opinion.”

title: Israel's Epic Fail: Fake Gods & Big Problems

paragraphs: “Yo, blow the trumpet! Sound the alarm! Vultures are literally circling over God’s people because they completely broke my covenant and ignored my rules. And what’s their response? They cry out, ‘My God! We know you!’ but their actions are screaming the opposite. Israel wants nothing to do with what’s good, and now the enemy is hot on their trail.

They’re crowning kings without even asking me. They set up princes but totally left me out of the loop. Instead, they’re making idols from their silver and gold, and those very idols are gonna be their downfall. Just throw that gold calf-god on the trash heap, Samaria! I’m seething with anger against that rubbish! How long until they finally get it together? And they’re supposed to be Israelites! A sculptor made that thing — it’s not God. That Samaritan calf is going to be broken to bits. Look at them! They’re planting wind-seeds, and they’re about to harvest a whole tornado. Their wheat has no head, so it makes no flour. And even if it did, strangers would just come and wolf it down. Israel is swallowed up and spit right back out. Among the other nations, they’re seen as a piece of junk. They ran off to Assyria — like, seriously? Even wild donkeys stick with their own kind, but Ephraim is out there paying to get lovers. Now, because of their promiscuous life among the pagans, I’m going to gather them all and confront them. They’re about to reap the consequences and feel what it’s like to be crushed by a powerful king.

Ephraim has built a ton of altars, and then he turns around and uses them for sinning. Can you even believe that? Altars for sinning! I write out my revelation for them in super clear detail, and they act like they can’t even read it. They offer sacrifices to me and then just feast on the meat themselves. God is not pleased. I’m fed up — I’ll keep remembering their guilt. I’m going to punish their sins and send them straight back to Egypt. Israel has forgotten his Maker and gotten busy building palaces. Judah has gone all-in on building fortress cities. Well, I’m sending fire on their cities to burn down every single one of their fortifications.”

title: Party's Over, Israel. Payday's Here.

paragraphs: Don’t waste your life in wild orgies, Israel. Don’t party away your life with the heathen. You walk away from your God at the drop of a hat and like a prostitute sell yourself promiscuously at every sex-and-religion party on the street.

All that party food isn't going to satisfy you. You'll just end up feeling more empty. Seriously, you won't last in God's country at this rate. Some of you will end up broke in Egypt, others will get a harsh reality check in Assyria. As refugees, you won't get to worship God much—you'll be on basic rations, and your souls will get tainted by the spiritually toxic air. You'll be starving for a real connection with God, exiled from His land. Think you'll miss the holy days then? Bet you'll be homesick for the big festivals.

But watch out. When you think you've escaped one disaster, you'll land right in another one in Egypt. And Egypt will be the one throwing your funeral! What good will all your precious silver be then, when you're just trying to survive in a field full of weeds?

Time’s up. Doom’s at the doorstep. It’s payday! Did Israel bluster, “The prophet is crazy! The ‘man of the Spirit’ is nuts!”? Think again. Because of your great guilt, you’re in big trouble. The prophet is looking out for Ephraim, working under God’s orders. But everyone is trying to trip him up. He’s hated right in God’s house, of all places. The people are going from bad to worse, rivaling that ancient and unspeakable crime at Gibeah. God’s keeping track of their guilt. He’ll make them pay for their sins.

“A long time ago, when I first found Israel, it was like discovering grapes in the middle of a desert. Finding your ancestors was like finding the first figs of the season. But when they arrived at Baal-peor, that pagan shrine, they took to sin like a pig to filth, wallowing in the mud with their newfound friends. Ephraim is fickle and scattered, like a flock of blackbirds, their beauty dissipated in confusion and clamor. Frenetic and noisy, frigid and barren, and nothing to show for it — neither conception nor childbirth.

And even if they managed to have kids, I'd have to say they're unfit parents and take them away. Seriously, it'll be a dark day for them when I just turn my back and walk away. I see Ephraim letting his kids run wild. He might as well be leading them straight to their own destruction!"
God, give them what they deserve! But what? Give them wombs that can't have kids and dried-up breasts.

"All their evil was exposed at that pagan shrine in Gilgal. Man, I hated them for that. Because of all their messed-up actions, I'm kicking them out of my land. I'm done wasting my love on them. Their leaders are just a bunch of rebellious teens. Ephraim is toast—roots dried up, no more fruit. And even if, by some miracle, they had kids, those precious babies wouldn't survive. I'd make sure of it!"
My God has washed his hands of them. They wouldn’t listen. They’re doomed to be wanderers, vagabonds among the godless nations.

title: Israel's Epic Fail: Fake Worship & Broken Promises

paragraphs: Israel was like a super productive vine, always loaded with grapes. But the more successful they got, the more they messed around with fake gods. The richer they became, the more cash they blew on idols they made up themselves. Their friendly smiles are totally fake. They're 100% guilty. God's about to smash their little worship spots and grind their statues into dust.

Then they'll be like, “A king? Who needs one? We don't even care about God, so why would a king matter? What could he even do for us?” They talk a big game, tell a bunch of lies, and make empty promises. But all their talk is just trash blowing in the wind.

The folks in Samaria are heading over to 'Crime City' to worship a golden calf idol. They're making a huge scene, dancing and shouting, totally fooled by their show-off priests. They act all important around this calf statue, but they have no idea it's all a scam and a total embarrassment. They're even planning to ship it to Assyria as a gift for the big king. That's how Ephraim is making a clown of himself, and Israel is getting shamed by its dumb idols.

Samaria is done for. Its king is like a dead branch floating down the river. And all of Israel's favorite places to sin will be destroyed. Thistles and crabgrass will decorate their ruined altars. Then they'll be screaming at the mountains, “Bury us!” and begging the hills, “Fall on us!”

You guys have been sinning since day one at Gibeah — that crazy, messed-up, ancient sin — and you just never stopped. So a war is coming to Gibeah to put an end to all this sinning. I’m going to show up and teach them a lesson. Nations will gang up on them, making them learn the hard way the sum of Gibeah plus Gibeah.

Ephraim was a trained heifer that loved to thresh. Passing by and seeing her strong, sleek neck, I wanted to harness Ephraim, put Ephraim to work in the fields — with Judah plowing and Jacob harrowing: ‘Sow righteousness, reap love. It’s time to till the ready earth, it’s time to dig in with God, until he arrives with righteousness ripe for harvest.’ But instead, you plowed wicked ways, reaped a crop of evil and ate a salad of lies. You thought you could do it all on your own, flush with weapons and manpower. But the volcano of war will erupt among your people. All your defense posts will be leveled as viciously as king Shalman leveled the town of Beth-arba, when mothers and their babies were smashed on the rocks. That’s what’s ahead for you, you so-called people of God, because of your off-the-charts evil. Some morning you’re going to wake up and find Israel, king and kingdom, a blank — nothing.

title: God's Uncancelable Love
changes: Ch11: msg_ranges normalized to MSG units [1-9, 10-12]; splits declared (1-9->[p0,p1,p2], 10-12->[p3,p4])
Ch11 p1: 'rescued him from getting stuck' -> 'rescued him from human bondage' (MSG); 'giving him a ride' -> 'pulling his wagon' (MSG)
Ch11 p2: 'right here with you' -> "in your very midst" (MSG)
paragraphs: “When Israel was just a kid, I loved him so much. I called him out of Egypt, like, ‘That’s my son!’ But the more other people called his name, the more he ran away from me. He started worshipping all the popular fake gods and messing around with idols.

Still, I was the one who stuck by him. I taught Ephraim how to walk, I rescued him from human bondage. But he never even gave me a shout-out, never admitted I was the one pulling his wagon, lifting him up like a baby to my cheek, and bending down to feed him. Now he wants to go back to Egypt or run off to Assyria — literally anywhere but back to me! That’s why his cities are a total mess, the murder rate is insane, and every plan they make just falls apart. My people are just hell-bent on leaving me. They’re praying to this Baal guy for help, but he’s not lifting a finger for them.

But for real, how can I just give up on you, Ephraim? How can I let you go, Israel? How could I ever let you get wrecked like Admah or destroyed like Zeboim? I can’t even stand the thought of it. My stomach is churning just thinking about it. So, I’m not gonna act on my anger. I’m not gonna destroy Ephraim. You know why? Because I’m God, not some human. I’m the Holy One, and I’m here — in your very midst.

“In the end, the people will follow God. I’ll roar like a lion—a massive roar! And my kids will come running back from the west, all scared and shaky. They’ll fly back from Egypt like frightened birds, and from Assyria like scared doves. And I’ll bring them all right back to their homes.” That’s God’s Word!
“Ephraim is all about lies, 24/7. You can’t trust a single thing Israel says. And Judah? No better. They’re addicted to cheap, fake gods.”

title: Don't Get Scammed by Fake Gods
changes: Ch12: msg_ranges normalized to MSG units [1-5, 6, 7-8, 9-11, 12-14]; splits declared (1-5->[p0,p1])
Ch12 p0: "get on Egypt's good side" -> 'tried to get an inside track with Egypt' (MSG)
Ch12 p1: 'God put him in his place' -> 'God bested him' (MSG)
Ch12 p4: "'But hold up'" -> "'But not so fast,'" (MSG)
paragraphs: Ephraim is all about chasing fantasies, like they’re trying to catch ghosts or something. They’re constantly telling lies, the kind that really mess with your soul. Both Ephraim and Judah tried to make deals with Assyria and tried to get an inside track with Egypt.

God’s basically taking Israel to court. Jacob’s descendants are getting called out and punished for their actions. Back in the womb, Jacob, that little heel, totally got one over on his brother. And when he grew up, he tried to pull the same thing on God. But you can’t outplay God. God bested him. Jacob ended up on his knees, crying and praying. God met him at Bethel, and that’s where they had a real talk. God is the God of Angel Armies, the God who reveals Himself, the God we can know.
So what are you even waiting for? Go back to your God! Be all about love and justice. Wait for your God, and don't ever give up on him!

The business guys are running a total scam. They love ripping people off! Ephraim was bragging, “Yo, I'm rich! I made it! And I'm so good at covering my tracks, you can't find a single trace of scamming or sin!”

“But not so fast,” says God, “I’m your God, the one who was with you back in Egypt! I’m gonna make you live in tents again, just like the old days when you used to worship in the desert. I speak through the prophets to show you what’s really going on. I use them to tell stories that reveal the truth. I’m showing how Gilead is a hotbed of religious drama and Gilgal is full of empty-headed religion. Their so-called worship spots are just like stinking piles of trash in their own backyards.”

Are you seriously going to be like your ancestor Jacob? He ran away to Aram all guilty, then basically sold his soul to get rich, making it big through lies and scams. Your true identity comes from the prophets God sent, the ones who led you out of Egypt and were like faithful pastors to you. But Ephraim has just kept on disrespecting God, no excuses. Now he's gotta pay the price for his destructive lifestyle. His Master is going to give him a taste of his own medicine.

title: God's Done Playing Games
changes: Ch13: msg_ranges normalized to MSG units [1-3, 4-6, 7-12, 13-15, 15-16] (MSG 13-15/15-16 overlap kept)
Ch13 p0: restored omitted ending 'like scraps of paper blown down the street, like smoke in a gusty wind' (KO had it, EN didn't)
Ch13 p1: added missing closing quote
Ch13 p2: restored omitted 'I'll rip out their guts. Coyotes will make a meal of them. Crows will clean their bones.' (KO had it, EN didn't)

Ch13 p3: removed added 'Nah' (not in MSG, changes meaning); rewritten around MSG 'Shall I intervene and pull them into life? ... Who is afraid of you, Death? ... abolishing regret, banishing sorrow'; removed added 'a storm is coming' (tornado starts in p4)
Ch13 p4: 'cities will be trashed' -> 'The cities will be gutted' (MSG); 'pregnant women attacked' -> 'pregnant women ripped open' (MSG)
paragraphs: God once let loose against Ephraim a terrifying sentence: caught and convicted in the lewd sex-worship of Baal — they died! And now they’re back in the sin business again, manufacturing god-images they can use, religion customized to taste. Professionals see to it: anything you want in a god you can get. Can you believe it? They sacrifice live babies to these dead gods — kill living babies and kiss golden calves! And now there’s nothing left of these people: hollow men, desiccated women, like scraps of paper blown down the street, like smoke in a gusty wind.

God’s like, “Yo, I’m still your God, the one who got you out of Egypt. I’m the only real God you’ve ever known, the only one who actually saves you. I took care of you during the hard desert years when you had nothing. I took care of you, took care of all your needs, gave you everything you needed. You got spoiled. You thought you didn’t need me. You straight-up forgot me.”

“I’ll charge them like a lion, like a leopard stalking in the brush. I’ll jump them like a sow grizzly robbed of her cubs. I’ll rip out their guts. Coyotes will make a meal of them. Crows will clean their bones. I’m going to destroy you, Israel. Who is going to stop me? Where is your trusty king you thought would save you? Where are all the local leaders you wanted so badly? All these rulers you insisted on having, demanding, ‘Give me a king! Give me leaders!’? Well, long ago I gave you a king, but I wasn’t happy about it. Now, fed up, I’ve gotten rid of him. I have a detailed record of your infidelities — Ephraim’s sin documented and stored in a safe-deposit box.”

“When birth pangs signaled it was time to be born, Ephraim was too stupid to come out of the womb. When the passage into life opened up, he didn’t show. Shall I intervene and pull them into life? Shall I snatch them from a certain death? Who is afraid of you, Death? Who cares about your threats, Tomb? In the end I’m abolishing regret, banishing sorrow, even though Ephraim ran wild, the black sheep of the family.”

“God’s tornado is on its way, roaring out of the desert. It will devastate the country, leaving a trail of ruin and wreckage. The cities will be gutted, dear possessions gone for good. Now Samaria has to face the charges because she has rebelled against her God: her people will be killed, babies smashed on the rocks, pregnant women ripped open.”

title: The Ultimate Comeback Story
changes: Ch14: msg_ranges normalized to MSG units [1-3, 4-8, 9]
Ch14 p0: 'Our promises to change are the real deal' -> 'Receive as restitution our repentant prayers' (MSG)
Ch14 p1: "I'm the one who's got his back" -> "I'm the one who answers and satisfies him" (MSG); kept 'vintage children of God'
paragraphs: Come back, Israel! Return to your God! You’re down but you’re not out. Prepare your confession and come back to God. Pray to him: ‘Take away our sin, accept our confession. Receive as restitution our repentant prayers. Assyria won’t save us; horses won’t get us where we want to go. We’ll never again call something we made ‘our god.’ You’re our last hope. Is it not true that in you the orphan finds mercy?’

God’s like, ‘I’m going to fix their rebellious streak. I’m gonna love them like crazy. I’m not mad anymore. It’s a clean slate for Israel. They’re gonna blossom like a crocus in spring and put down deep oak tree roots — they’ll become a forest of oaks! They’ll be amazing, like a giant sequoia, and smell as good as a grove of cedars. The people living near them will be blessed because of them, and they’ll thrive like golden grain. Everyone will be talking about them, spreading their fame as the vintage children of God. Ephraim is so over those fake gods. From now on, I’m the one who answers and satisfies him. I’m like a tree that’s always loaded with fruit. Everything you could ever need, you can find in me.’

If you want to live a good life, you gotta understand this. If you know what's good for you, you'll learn this stuff by heart. God's ways are the right ways to go. People who live right can walk them no problem, but people who do wrong are always tripping over themselves.
